title: Bathroom sink stopper repair: pop-up assembly diagnosis, seal, and reassembly

locations.name: Bathroom sink area (probable)
locations.basis: The video topic is a bathroom sink stopper; no explicit shooting location is given in transcript.

summary: An experienced craftsman guides viewers through diagnosing a stuck bathroom sink stopper, disassembling the pop-up assembly, removing and replacing a rotted strainer and tailpiece, applying plumber's putty and pipe dope to seal the drain, trimming the tailpiece to fit, and reassembling the linkage with a rod and clip while ensuring correct alignment perpendicular to the back wall, finishing with a functional test of the stopper.
topics: holding strainer with screwdrivers to loosen nut
swiveling nut to allow through-wall clearance

sections.title: Diagnose and disassemble pop-up stopper
sections.description: The presenter identifies a bound-up linkage, opens the pop-up assembly, and notes that the stopper linkage is broken, initiating disassembly of the tailpiece and strainer to access the assembly.

sections.title: Seal drain assembly and prepare connection
sections.description: Plumber's putty is formed into a ring and pressed into place, a gasket is seated from the bottom, and pipe dope is applied for a tight seal. The tailpiece is planned and cut to fit, with emphasis on aligning the connection perpendicular to the back wall.

sections.title: Reassemble linkage and test
sections.description: The tailpiece is finally adjusted, a rod and clip are installed to secure the linkage, the stopper is inserted and aligned, and a test confirms the stopper moves up and down properly.

featured_techniques.technique: Inspecting and diagnosing a stuck pop-up stopper linkage
Disassembling a pop-up stopper and strainer assembly and removing the tailpiece
Sealing the drain with plumber's putty and gasket; applying pipe dope
Cutting tailpiece to length and aligning perpendicular to the back wall
Swiveling and tightening the through-wall connection and compression nut
Installing rod and clip to secure linkage and ensure smooth operation
